scene.label: Act 2, Scene 1
scene.title: SCENE I. Pentapolis. An open place by the seaside.
scene.location: Pentapolis. An open place by the seaside.

lines.text: Yet cease your ire, you angry stars of heaven!
lines.plainText: Yet cease your ire you angry stars of heaven

lines.text: Wind, rain, and thunder, remember earthly man
lines.plainText: Wind rain and thunder remember earthly man

lines.text: Is but a substance that must yield to you;
lines.plainText: Is but a substance that must yield to you

lines.text: And I, as fits my nature, do obey you:
lines.plainText: And I as fits my nature do obey you

lines.text: Alas, the sea hath cast me on the rocks,
lines.plainText: Alas the sea hath cast me on the rocks

lines.text: Wash'd me from shore to shore, and left me breath
lines.plainText: Wash'd me from shore to shore and left me breath

lines.text: Nothing to think on but ensuing death:
lines.plainText: Nothing to think on but ensuing death

lines.text: Let it suffice the greatness of your powers
lines.plainText: Let it suffice the greatness of your powers

lines.text: To have bereft a prince of all his fortunes;
lines.plainText: To have bereft a prince of all his fortunes

lines.text: And having thrown him from your watery grave,
lines.plainText: And having thrown him from your watery grave

lines.text: Here to have death in peace is all he'll crave.
lines.plainText: Here to have death in peace is all he'll crave

lines.text: What, ho, Pilch!
lines.plainText: What ho Pilch

lines.text: Ha, come and bring away the nets!
lines.plainText: Ha come and bring away the nets

lines.text: What, Patch-breech, I say!
lines.plainText: What Patchbreech I say

lines.text: What say you, master?
lines.plainText: What say you master

lines.text: Look how thou stirrest now! Come away, or I'll fetch thee with a wanion.
lines.plainText: Look how thou stirrest now Come away or I'll fetch thee with a wanion

lines.text: Faith, master, I am thinking of the poor men that were cast away before us even now.
lines.plainText: Faith master I am thinking of the poor men that were cast away before us even now

lines.text: Alas, poor souls, it grieved my heart to hear what pitiful cries they made to us to help them, when, well-a-day, we could scarce help ourselves.
lines.plainText: Alas poor souls it grieved my heart to hear what pitiful cries they made to us to help them when welladay we could scarce help ourselves

lines.text: Nay, master, said not I as much when I saw the porpus how he bounced and tumbled? They say they're half fish, half flesh: a plague on them, they ne'er come but I look to be washed. Master, I marvel how the fishes live in the sea.
lines.plainText: Nay master said not I as much when I saw the porpus how he bounced and tumbled They say they're half fish half flesh a plague on them they ne'er come but I look to be washed Master I marvel how the fishes live in the sea

lines.text: Why, as men do a-land; the great ones eat up the little ones: I can compare our rich misers to nothing so fitly as to a whale; a' plays and tumbles, driving the poor fry before him, and at last devours them all at a mouthful. Such whales have I heard on o' the land, who never leave gaping till they swallowed the whole parish, church, steeple, bells and all.
lines.plainText: Why as men do aland the great ones eat up the little ones I can compare our rich misers to nothing so fitly as to a whale a' plays and tumbles driving the poor fry before him and at last devours them all at a mouthful Such whales have I heard on o' the land who never leave gaping till they swallowed the whole parish church steeple bells and all

lines.text: [Aside.] A pretty moral.
lines.plainText: Aside A pretty moral

lines.text: But, master, if I had been the sexton, I would have been that day in the belfry.
lines.plainText: But master if I had been the sexton I would have been that day in the belfry

lines.text: Why, man?
lines.plainText: Why man

lines.text: Because he should have swallowed me too; and when I had been in his belly, I would have kept such a jangling of the bells, that he should never have left, till he cast bells, steeple, church and parish up again. But if the good King Simonides were of my mind,—
lines.plainText: Because he should have swallowed me too and when I had been in his belly I would have kept such a jangling of the bells that he should never have left till he cast bells steeple church and parish up again But if the good King Simonides were of my mind

lines.text: [Aside.] Simonides?
lines.plainText: Aside Simonides

lines.text: We would purge the land of these drones, that rob the bee of her honey.
lines.plainText: We would purge the land of these drones that rob the bee of her honey

lines.text: [Aside.] How from the finny subject of the sea
lines.plainText: Aside How from the finny subject of the sea

lines.text: These fishers tell the infirmities of men;
lines.plainText: These fishers tell the infirmities of men

lines.text: And from their watery empire recollect
lines.plainText: And from their watery empire recollect

lines.text: All that may men approve or men detect!
lines.plainText: All that may men approve or men detect

lines.text: Peace be at your labour, honest fishermen.
lines.plainText: Peace be at your labour honest fishermen

lines.text: Honest! good fellow, what's that? If it be a day fits you, search out of the calendar, and nobody look after it.
lines.plainText: Honest good fellow what's that If it be a day fits you search out of the calendar and nobody look after it

lines.text: May see the sea hath cast upon your coast.
lines.plainText: May see the sea hath cast upon your coast

lines.text: What a drunken knave was the sea to cast thee in our way!
lines.plainText: What a drunken knave was the sea to cast thee in our way

lines.text: A man whom both the waters and the wind,
lines.plainText: A man whom both the waters and the wind

lines.text: In that vast tennis-court, have made the ball
lines.plainText: In that vast tenniscourt have made the ball

lines.text: For them to play upon, entreats you pity him;
lines.plainText: For them to play upon entreats you pity him

lines.text: He asks of you, that never used to beg.
lines.plainText: He asks of you that never used to beg

lines.text: No, friend, cannot you beg? Here's them in our country of Greece gets more with begging than we can do with working.
lines.plainText: No friend cannot you beg Here's them in our country of Greece gets more with begging than we can do with working

lines.text: Canst thou catch any fishes, then?
lines.plainText: Canst thou catch any fishes then

lines.text: I never practised it.
lines.plainText: I never practised it

lines.text: Nay, then thou wilt starve, sure; for here's nothing to be got now-a-days, unless thou canst fish for't.
lines.plainText: Nay then thou wilt starve sure for here's nothing to be got nowadays unless thou canst fish for't

lines.text: What I have been I have forgot to know;
lines.plainText: What I have been I have forgot to know

lines.text: But what I am, want teaches me to think on:
lines.plainText: But what I am want teaches me to think on

lines.text: A man throng'd up with cold: my veins are chill,
lines.plainText: A man throng'd up with cold my veins are chill

lines.text: And have no more of life than may suffice
lines.plainText: And have no more of life than may suffice

lines.text: To give my tongue that heat to ask your help;
lines.plainText: To give my tongue that heat to ask your help

lines.text: Which if you shall refuse, when I am dead,
lines.plainText: Which if you shall refuse when I am dead

lines.text: For that I am a man, pray see me buried.
lines.plainText: For that I am a man pray see me buried

lines.text: Die quoth-a? Now gods forbid't, and I have a gown here; come, put it on; keep thee warm. Now, afore me, a handsome fellow! Come, thou shalt go home, and we'll have flesh for holidays, fish for fasting-days, and moreo'er puddings and flap-jacks, and thou shalt be welcome.
lines.plainText: Die quotha Now gods forbid't and I have a gown here come put it on keep thee warm Now afore me a handsome fellow Come thou shalt go home and we'll have flesh for holidays fish for fastingdays and moreo'er puddings and flapjacks and thou shalt be welcome

lines.text: I thank you, sir.
lines.plainText: I thank you sir

lines.text: Hark you, my friend; you said you could not beg?
lines.plainText: Hark you my friend you said you could not beg

lines.text: I did but crave.
lines.plainText: I did but crave

lines.text: But crave! Then I'll turn craver too, and so I shall 'scape whipping.
lines.plainText: But crave Then I'll turn craver too and so I shall 'scape whipping

lines.text: Why, are your beggars whipped, then?
lines.plainText: Why are your beggars whipped then

lines.text: O, not all, my friend, not all; for if all your beggars were whipped, I would wish no better office than to be beadle. But, master, I'll go draw up the net.
lines.plainText: O not all my friend not all for if all your beggars were whipped I would wish no better office than to be beadle But master I'll go draw up the net

lines.text: [Aside.] How well this honest mirth becomes their labour!
lines.plainText: Aside How well this honest mirth becomes their labour

lines.text: Hark you, sir, do you know where ye are?
lines.plainText: Hark you sir do you know where ye are

lines.text: Not well.
lines.plainText: Not well

lines.text: Why, I'll tell you: this is called Pentapolis, and our King, the good Simonides.
lines.plainText: Why I'll tell you this is called Pentapolis and our King the good Simonides

lines.text: The good Simonides, do you call him?
lines.plainText: The good Simonides do you call him

lines.text: Ay, sir; and he deserves so to be called for his peaceable reign and good government.
lines.plainText: Ay sir and he deserves so to be called for his peaceable reign and good government

lines.text: He is a happy king, since he gains from his subjects the name of good government. How far is his court distant from this shore?
lines.plainText: He is a happy king since he gains from his subjects the name of good government How far is his court distant from this shore

lines.text: Marry sir, half a day's journey: and I'll tell you, he hath a fair daughter, and tomorrow is her birth-day; and there are princes and knights come from all parts of the world to joust and tourney for her love.
lines.plainText: Marry sir half a day's journey and I'll tell you he hath a fair daughter and tomorrow is her birthday and there are princes and knights come from all parts of the world to joust and tourney for her love

lines.text: Were my fortunes equal to my desires, I could wish to make one there.
lines.plainText: Were my fortunes equal to my desires I could wish to make one there

lines.text: O, sir, things must be as they may; and what a man cannot get, he may lawfully deal for—his wife's soul.
lines.plainText: O sir things must be as they may and what a man cannot get he may lawfully deal forhis wife's soul

content.text: Re-enter Second and Third Fishermen, drawing up a net.

lines.text: Help, master, help! here's a fish hangs in the net, like a poor man's right in the law; 'twill hardly come out. Ha! bots on't, 'tis come at last, and 'tis turned to a rusty armour.
lines.plainText: Help master help here's a fish hangs in the net like a poor man's right in the law 'twill hardly come out Ha bots on't 'tis come at last and 'tis turned to a rusty armour

lines.text: An armour, friends! I pray you, let me see it.
lines.plainText: An armour friends I pray you let me see it

lines.text: Thanks, Fortune, yet, that, after all my crosses,
lines.plainText: Thanks Fortune yet that after all my crosses

lines.text: Thou givest me somewhat to repair myself,
lines.plainText: Thou givest me somewhat to repair myself

lines.text: And though it was mine own, part of my heritage,
lines.plainText: And though it was mine own part of my heritage

lines.text: Which my dead father did bequeath to me,
lines.plainText: Which my dead father did bequeath to me

lines.text: With this strict charge, even as he left his life.
lines.plainText: With this strict charge even as he left his life

lines.text: 'Keep it, my Pericles; it hath been a shield
lines.plainText: 'Keep it my Pericles it hath been a shield

lines.text: 'Twixt me and death;'—and pointed to this brace;—
lines.plainText: 'Twixt me and death'and pointed to this brace

lines.text: 'For that it saved me, keep it; in like necessity—
lines.plainText: 'For that it saved me keep it in like necessity

lines.text: The which the gods protect thee from!—may defend thee.'
lines.plainText: The which the gods protect thee frommay defend thee'

lines.text: It kept where I kept, I so dearly loved it;
lines.plainText: It kept where I kept I so dearly loved it

lines.text: Till the rough seas, that spares not any man,
lines.plainText: Till the rough seas that spares not any man

lines.text: Took it in rage, though calm'd have given't again:
lines.plainText: Took it in rage though calm'd have given't again

lines.text: I thank thee for't: my shipwreck now's no ill,
lines.plainText: I thank thee for't my shipwreck now's no ill

lines.text: Since I have here my father gave in his will.
lines.plainText: Since I have here my father gave in his will

lines.text: What mean you sir?
lines.plainText: What mean you sir

lines.text: To beg of you, kind friends, this coat of worth,
lines.plainText: To beg of you kind friends this coat of worth

lines.text: For it was sometime target to a king;
lines.plainText: For it was sometime target to a king

lines.text: I know it by this mark. He loved me dearly,
lines.plainText: I know it by this mark He loved me dearly

lines.text: And for his sake I wish the having of it;
lines.plainText: And for his sake I wish the having of it

lines.text: And that you'd guide me to your sovereign court,
lines.plainText: And that you'd guide me to your sovereign court

lines.text: Where with it I may appear a gentleman;
lines.plainText: Where with it I may appear a gentleman

lines.text: And if that ever my low fortune's better,
lines.plainText: And if that ever my low fortune's better

lines.text: I'll pay your bounties; till then rest your debtor.
lines.plainText: I'll pay your bounties till then rest your debtor

lines.text: Why, wilt thou tourney for the lady?
lines.plainText: Why wilt thou tourney for the lady

lines.text: I'll show the virtue I have borne in arms.
lines.plainText: I'll show the virtue I have borne in arms

lines.text: Why, d'ye take it, and the gods give thee good on't!
lines.plainText: Why d'ye take it and the gods give thee good on't

lines.text: Ay, but hark you, my friend; 'twas we that made up this garment through the rough seams of the waters: there are certain condolements, certain vails. I hope, sir, if you thrive, you'll remember from whence you had them.
lines.plainText: Ay but hark you my friend 'twas we that made up this garment through the rough seams of the waters there are certain condolements certain vails I hope sir if you thrive you'll remember from whence you had them

lines.text: Believe't I will.
lines.plainText: Believe't I will

lines.plainText: By your furtherance I am clothed in steel

lines.text: And spite of all the rapture of the sea,
lines.plainText: And spite of all the rapture of the sea

lines.plainText: This jewel holds his building on my arm

lines.plainText: Unto thy value I will mount myself

lines.plainText: Upon a courser whose delightful steps

lines.text: Shall make the gazer joy to see him tread.
lines.plainText: Shall make the gazer joy to see him tread

lines.text: Of a pair of bases.
